alerts.title: TDF nephrotoxicity vs dehydration-induced AKI
alerts.message: Guidelines list acute kidney injury as a major toxicity of TDF. Patient has severe creatinine rise (0.9 to 2.4) with urea:creatinine ratio 24:1, favouring pre-renal dehydration from gastroenteritis. Two household contacts share the illness, supporting infectious gastroenteritis. Urinalysis shows no protein or glucose, which argues against TDF-induced tubular injury (Fanconi syndrome). TDF can cause AKI directly, but the clinical picture—dehydration, hypotension, hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia—strongly supports pre-renal AKI from volume loss. TDF may compound renal stress during dehydration. Stopping TDF permanently may be premature without first resuscitating and reassessing renal recovery.

evidence.recommended_action: Resuscitate with IV fluids and reassess creatinine after hydration. Consider temporary TDF hold during acute illness, but do not permanently discontinue without confirming renal recovery post-resuscitation.

alerts.title: Premature permanent TDF discontinuation plan
alerts.message: Clinician plans to stop TDF permanently due to AKI. Guidelines recognise TDF can cause AKI, but this patient's AKI is most likely pre-renal from severe dehydration (urea:creatinine ratio 24:1, hypotension, gastroenteritis). Permanent discontinuation is premature before renal recovery is assessed post-resuscitation. Unnecessary switching could compromise a suppressed regimen (viral load <50) and limit future options. A temporary hold during acute illness with reassessment is more appropriate.

evidence.recommended_action: Hold TDF temporarily during acute kidney injury, resuscitate, then reassess creatinine. Only consider permanent switch if renal function does not recover after correction of dehydration.

alerts.title: TDF renal monitoring gap during acute illness
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring every 12 months for patients on TDF. Patient's last documented creatinine was 2025-02-14, over 12 months ago. The current creatinine (2.4) was only checked because of acute presentation. Additionally, no eGFR has been documented. During acute kidney injury, ongoing serial creatinine monitoring is essential to track recovery or deterioration after resuscitation.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor serial creatinine and eGFR daily during acute illness, then every 3 months until stable. Ensure routine 12-monthly TDF renal monitoring resumes after recovery.
